canonical_name: Strong perfect graph theorem family for finite simple graphs
literal_source_claim_zh: 完美图的禁用子图刻画
statement_blocker: The inspected primary source identifies Theorem 1.2 as perfect iff Berge for finite simple graphs, but no independently accepted source record yet freezes the incorporated definitions and proof boundary. The Lean target must still choose exact induced-subgraph quantification, ENat/Nat chromatic-number transport, clique-number coercion, chordless odd-hole and odd-antihole encodings, complement transport, typeclasses, binders, and boundary cases. Selecting an expression at intake would bypass the assigned statement phase.
target_decision: preserve the source-backed strong-perfect-graph theorem family and require independent source acceptance plus exact encoding freeze in the statement phase
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted statement must quantify over finite simple graphs and fix the vertex type universe, Fintype versus Finite presentation, decidable equality and adjacency boundary, and induced-subgraph representation.
conclusion: Open formal encoding of the source theorem that a finite simple graph is perfect if and only if it is Berge, equivalently that perfect graphs are exactly those with no odd hole or odd antihole.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before the exact proposition is frozen; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md without silently adding source-external hypotheses.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Perfect G iff Berge G, with Perfect quantifying over all induced subgraphs and Berge excluding odd holes and odd antiholes
a direct forbidden-induced-subgraph statement excluding odd cycles of length at least five in G and its complement
a formulation over finite graph structures rather than Fintype-indexed SimpleGraph
the easy direction Perfect G implies Berge G
the hard direction Berge G implies Perfect G
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty induced vertex subsets and preservation of finiteness under induce
complete and edgeless graphs, bipartite graphs, and complements
cycles of length three, four, five, and even or odd larger lengths
chorded cycles versus induced chordless cycles
ENat-valued chromatic number versus Nat-valued clique number and exclusion of top
excluded_substitutions: the weak perfect graph theorem that complements preserve perfectness
only Perfect implies Berge or only Berge implies Perfect
excluding ordinary odd cycles instead of induced odd holes
excluding only odd holes or only odd antiholes
a theorem only for bipartite, chordal, comparability, or another specialized graph class
perfect matching, perfect group, perfect field, PerfectRing, or strongly regular graph results
a structure or hypothesis that stores the desired perfection or forbidden-subgraph conclusion

source_candidates_not_credited.citation: Maria Chudnovsky, Neil Robertson, Paul Seymour, and Robin Thomas, The strong perfect graph theorem, Annals of Mathematics 164(1) (2006), 51-229
source_candidates_not_credited.candidate_locator: abstract and article pages 51-52 for definitions and Theorem 1.2; article pages 52-229 for proof
source_candidates_not_credited.candidate_summary: For finite simple graphs, perfect means every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to maximum-clique size; Berge excludes odd holes and odd antiholes; Theorem 1.2 states perfect iff Berge and the paper proves it.
source_candidates_not_credited.inspection_status: primary source lead inspected; repository-owned immutable preservation, complete incorporated-definition/premise/proof-node/correction crosswalk, and independent review remain open
